product_summary: Catalogue (suriepolex.com, About Us + full category tree) shows the company is an ABRASIVES manufacturer, not a stone/construction-materials supplier. Real product lines: (1) Marble polishing abrasives — magnesite abrasive, synthetic abrasives, Frankfurt abrasive, metal-bond diamond for marble, resin-bond diamond for marble, edge-polishing abrasives, chamfering/finishing brushes, marble polishing pads; (2) Granite — metal fickert, resin fickert, lux fickert, fickert brushes, diamond pads, 8" plate, grinding & cutting tools; (3) Concrete — metal-bond diamond grinding tools, grinding tools for its own and third-party machines, hand/ride-on trowels; (4) Engineered quartz — metal/resin bond diamond; (5) Metal & stone cutting wheels — cutting wheel, DC grinding wheel, WA grinding wheel, flap disc, GC wheel, engraving tools, profile diamond wheel; (6) Machines — marble/granite/concrete polishing machines, single-disc machines, floor polishing machines, dust collectors & vacuums, concrete laying machines; (7) Chemicals — marble adhesive, epoxy, sealer, densifier, wax polish, polishing powders, cleaners, stain removers, concrete colour dye. Declared 6804.21 (millstones/grindstones of agglomerated synthetic or natural diamond) is genuinely present in the range (metal-bond and resin-bond diamond abrasives for marble/granite/quartz), so the declaration is not wrong — but it covers only a fraction of the line.
comment: MATCH: partial. 6804.21 is corroborated by the company's own catalogue (diamond-bond abrasives for marble/granite/quartz) — declared code is correct for that segment, so no rejection and no HS correction needed for the declared line. However the declaration is materially incomplete: the same catalogue shows non-diamond bonded abrasives (magnesite, synthetic, Frankfurt, fickert) which fall under 6804.22/6804.23 rather than 6804.21, plus cutting/grinding wheels and discs (8202.39), diamond profile/engraving tools (8207.90), polishing/grinding machines and trowels (8464.20, 8479.89), and a full chemicals line — epoxy/adhesive (3506.91), sealers/densifiers (3824.99), wax polish (3405.90), cleaners (3405.90), concrete colour dye (3208.90). INDUSTRY MISCLASSIFICATION: claimed industry 'Строительство и DIY' (construction & DIY) is imprecise — the company is an abrasive-tool and surface-treatment manufacturer serving the stone-processing and concrete-flooring trades; it is not a construction-materials or DIY-retail supplier. Its own site describes it as 'at the forefront of the abrasive industry'. ENTITY-TYPE FLAG (not an HS matter, flagged for the registry team): the website consistently brands itself 'Surie Polex Industries LLP' and 'Surie Polex Industries LLP since 1985', while the batch record claims 'PRIVATE LIMITED'. The legal-form discrepancy between the claimed name and the company's own self-description is unresolved from public pages and should be checked against the MCA record — I did not research registries per scope. FACTUALITY: all product lines above are 'заявлено, не подтверждено' — they come from the company's own website catalogue and About page (https://www.suriepolex.com/ and https://www.suriepolex.com/about-us), not from any customs line. No shipment or customs record was examined in this task, so no product line can be marked as corroborated by a customs entry. Revenue, export volume, PAN, CIN and state: null — not public on the pages read and out of scope for this task.
